audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused EIPs (EIP-140 REVERT, Spurious Dragon state clearing/code size/EXP repricing, Cancun memory/stack operations, EIP-170 code size limit, EIP-7516 BLOBBASEFEE, EIP-1716 Petersburg hardfork) and CL-related EIPs (EIP-4736 BLSToExecutionChange broadcast, EIP-6916 testnet reset). EIP-7713 covers EIP-712 signing which spans wallet/contract boundaries.

in_scope: EVM Opcode Execution (REVERT, BLOBBASEFEE, EXP, MLOAD/MSTORE/MCOPY)
State Transition (account clearing, SSTORE gas metering)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component - transaction execution context is part of the EL, not an external entity
Internal EVM component - CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes are part of the EL execution engine
Internal EVM component - the bytecode interpreter is a core part of the EL
Internal to the user's signing flow - wallet software is the client-side component performing validation, not an external data source into the EL/CL
Internal EL component - a smart contract verifying signatures is part of the EL state machine

trusted_external_entities.name: User via Transaction (Contract Deployer)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (contract creation tx with init code)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit contract creation transactions. Init code and returned bytecode are arbitrary and untrusted. EIP-170 size limits and gas metering provide bounds on resource consumption.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via Transaction (General)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions trigger EVM execution including REVERT, memory operations, stack operations, and BLOBBASEFEE opcode. All user-supplied data (calldata, gas limits) is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via EIP-712 Signing Request
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EIP-712 eth_signTypedData RPC with box type extensions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps construct EIP-712 messages with boxed values. Malicious DApps could craft type schemas to confuse users or exploit type parsing. Inner type definitions and values are untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/Signer via Wallet Approval
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet signing approval for EIP-712 messages
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users may not fully understand boxed content implications. Signatures produced are valid but user intent may not match signed content. The user is external to the protocol verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via BLSToExecutionChange
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: BLSToExecutionChange message submission to community repository
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit withdrawal credential change claims. Claims require BLS signature verification. Attackers with compromised deposit keys may submit competing claims. No authentication beyond cryptographic signature.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator via Broadcast File Loading
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators voluntarily load broadcast files. Malicious or incorrect broadcast files could cause legitimate messages to be filtered. No protocol-level authentication of broadcast file contents.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer via Beacon Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes may send malicious or conflicting BLSToExecutionChange messages. No authentication on P2P layer. Broadcast file filtering provides defense but only for known validators.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer via Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate blocks containing contract creations, transactions triggering EVM opcodes. Blocks from untrusted peers must be fully validated including EIP-170 size checks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator Operator (Testnet)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker deposits validators to gain majority stake on testnet. Reset mechanism (EIP-6916) mitigates by clearing accumulated attacker progress. Fully untrusted entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Claim Submitter via Community Repository
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Community repository claim submission (e.g., GitHub PR)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anyone can submit BLSToExecutionChange claims to the community repository. Claims require cryptographic verification. Submitter identity is not authenticated beyond the BLS signature.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Init code is arbitrary and must execute within gas limits. Returned bytecode must be validated against MAX_CODE_SIZE (24576 bytes, EIP-170). Size violation triggers OOG consuming all gas.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM transaction execution (opcodes: REVERT, MLOAD, MSTORE, MCOPY, BLOBBASEFEE, EXP, stack ops)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All transaction parameters (gas, calldata) must be validated. EVM enforces gas limits, stack bounds (1024 max), memory expansion costs (quadratic), and REVERT state rollback. BLOBBASEFEE requires EIP-4844 activation.

Box type schemas must be validated: inner types must follow EIP-712 rules, type isolation must be enforced (inner types cannot reference outer types), and boxed contents must be rendered to user before signing approval.

Wallet must display decoded boxed contents to user. User must understand that boxed contents are cryptographically committed alongside outer struct. Opaque hex display defeats the purpose of EIP-7713.

BLS signature must be cryptographically verified. Validator index must correspond to active validator. Only one operation per validator index allowed. Contested claims require out-of-band social resolution.
Broadcast file contents should be sourced from verified community repository. Operator must verify file integrity. Malicious broadcast files could filter legitimate messages.

All incoming messages must be checked against broadcast file. Matching messages accepted, conflicting messages rejected. Messages for unknown validators accepted without protection. Full BLS signature re-verification required.
Blocks must be fully validated: all contract creations checked against EIP-170 size limit, all state transitions verified, gas accounting validated. Block validation must complete in bounded time.
Testnet reset period must be shorter than minimum takeover time (5.7 days for 10k validators). Genesis validator set must be sufficiently large. Reset mechanism clears attacker's accumulated stake.

Filename format validation, validator active status check, BLS signature verification, and single-operation-per-validator constraint must all pass. Community verification process must be honest and complete.
